**Nelson** ([Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language "Māori language"): _Whakatū_) is a [city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_New_Zealand "List of cities in New Zealand") and [unitary authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_New_Zealand "Districts of New Zealand") on the eastern shores of the [Tasman Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_Bay "Tasman Bay") at the top of the [South Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Island "South Island") of New Zealand. It is the oldest city in the South Island and the second-oldest settled city in the country; it was established in 1841 and became a city by British [royal charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter") in 1858.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-TeAra_places1-3)

Nelson City is bordered to the west and south-west by the [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District") and to the north-east, east and south-east by the [Marlborough District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_District "Marlborough District"). The Nelson urban area has a population of 50,800,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-NZ_population_data_2018-1) making it New Zealand's 15th [most populous urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_populated_places_in_New_Zealand "List of populated places in New Zealand").

Nelson is well known for its thriving local arts and crafts scene; each year, the city hosts events popular with locals and tourists alike, such as the Nelson Arts Festival.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-4)

## Naming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Naming")]

Nelson was named in honour of Admiral [Horatio Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Nelson,_1st_Viscount_Nelson "Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson"), who defeated both the [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_French_Empire "First French Empire") and [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") fleets at the [Battle of Trafalgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Trafalgar "Battle of Trafalgar") in October 1805. Many roads and public areas around the city are named after people and ships associated with that battle. Inhabitants of the city are referred to as "Nelsonians". Trafalgar Street is its main shopping axis.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Nelson's [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language "Māori language") name, _Whakatū_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Maori-5) means 'construct', 'raise', or 'establish'.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-6)

In an article to _The Colonist_ newspaper on 16 July 1867, Francis Stevens described Nelson as "The [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples") of the [Southern Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere "Southern Hemisphere")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-7) Today, Nelson is nicknamed "Sunny Nelson" due to its high sunshine hours per year and the "Top of the South" because of its geographic location.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [New Zealand Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Sign_Language "New Zealand Sign Language"), the name is signed by putting the index and middle fingers together, which are raised to the nose until the fingertips touch the nose, then move the hand forward so that the fingers point slightly forward away from oneself.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-8)

### Māori settlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Māori settlement")]

Settlement of Nelson began about 700 years ago by [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_people "Māori people").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-9) There is evidence that the earliest settlements in New Zealand were around the Nelson–Marlborough regions. Some of the earliest recorded [iwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iwi "Iwi") in the Nelson district are Ngāti Hāwea, Ngāti Wairangi, [Waitaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitaha_(South_Island_iwi) "Waitaha (South Island iwi)") and [Kāti Māmoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81ti_M%C4%81moe "Kāti Māmoe").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10) Waitaha people developed the land around the Waimea Gardens, are believed to have been the first people to quarry [argillite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argillite "Argillite") in around Nelson. They also developed much of the Waimea Gardens complex – more than 400 hectares (990 acres) on the Waimea Plains near Nelson.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Te_Tau-11) In the early 1600s, [Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_T%C5%ABmatak%C5%8Dkiri "Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri") displaced other [te Tau Ihu Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Tau_Ihu_M%C4%81ori "Te Tau Ihu Māori"), becoming the dominant tribe in the area until the early 1800s.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10) Raids from northern tribes in the 1820s, led by [Te Rauparaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Rauparaha "Te Rauparaha") and his [Ngāti Toa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Toa "Ngāti Toa"), soon decimated the local population and quickly displaced them.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Today, there are eight mutually recognised tribes of the northwestern region: [Ngāti Kuia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Kuia "Ngāti Kuia"), [Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Apa_ki_te_R%C4%81_T%C5%8D "Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō"), [Rangitāne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangit%C4%81ne "Rangitāne"), [Ngāti Toarangatira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Toa "Ngāti Toa"), [Ngāti Koata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Koata "Ngāti Koata"), [Ngāti Rārua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_R%C4%81rua "Ngāti Rārua"), [Ngāti Tama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Tama "Ngāti Tama") and [Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Atiawa_o_Te_Waka-a-M%C4%81ui "Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10)

### New Zealand Company and European settlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: New Zealand Company and European settlement")]

#### Planning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Planning")]

The [New Zealand Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Company "New Zealand Company") in London planned the settlement of Nelson. They intended to buy from the Māori some 200,000 acres (810 km 2) of land, which they planned to divide into one thousand lots and sell to intending settlers. The company earmarked profits to finance the free passage of [artisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artisan "Artisan") and [labourers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laborer "Laborer"), with their families, and for the construction of public works. However, by September 1841 only about one third of the lots had sold. Despite this, the colony pushed ahead, and land was surveyed by [Frederick Tuckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Tuckett "Frederick Tuckett").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-DNZB_Tuckett-12)

Three ships, the _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Arrow "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Whitby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Whitby "New Zealand Company ships")_, and _[Will Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Will\_Watch "New Zealand Company ships")_, sailed from London, the expedition commanded by Captain [Arthur Wakefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Wakefield "Arthur Wakefield"). Arriving in New Zealand, they discovered that the new Governor of the colony, [William Hobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hobson "William Hobson"), would not give them a free hand to secure vast areas of land from the Māori or indeed to decide where to site the colony. However, after some delay, Hobson allowed the company to investigate the Tasman Bay area at the north end of the South Island. The Company selected the site now occupied by Nelson City because it had the best harbour in the area. But it had a major drawback: it lacked suitable [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land "Arable land"); Nelson City stands right on the edge of a mountain range while the nearby Waimea Plains amount to only about 60,000 acres (240 km 2), less than one third of the area required by the Company plans.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Company secured land, which was not clearly defined, from the Māori for £800: it included Nelson, Waimea, [Motueka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motueka "Motueka"), [Riwaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riwaka "Riwaka") and Whakapuaka. This allowed the settlement to begin, but the lack of definition would prove the source of much future conflict. The three colony ships sailed into Nelson Haven during the first week of November 1841. When the first four immigrant ships – _[Fifeshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Fifeshire "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Mary-Ann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Mary\_Anne "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Lord Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Lord\_Auckland "New Zealand Company ships")_ and _[Lloyds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Lloyds "New Zealand Company ships")_ – arrived three months later, they found the town already laid out with streets, some wooden houses, tents and rough sheds. The town was laid out on a [grid plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan "Grid plan").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-13) Within 18 months, the company had sent out 18 ships with 1,052 men, 872 women and 1,384 children. However, fewer than ninety of the settlers had the capital to start as landowners.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### Cultural and religious immigrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cultural and religious immigrants")]

The early settlement of Nelson province included a proportion of [German immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_New_Zealanders "German New Zealanders"), who arrived on the ship _Sankt Pauli_ and formed the nucleus of the villages of Sarau ([Upper Moutere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Moutere "Upper Moutere")) and Neudorf. These were mostly [Lutheran Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism") with a small number of [Bavarian Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bavarians "Bavarians").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-14)

In 1892, the [New Zealand Church Missionary Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Church_Missionary_Society "New Zealand Church Missionary Society") (NZCMS) was formed in a Nelson church hall.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-NZCMS-Mission-15)

#### Problems with land

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Problems with land")]

After a brief initial period of prosperity, the lack of land and of capital caught up with the settlement and it entered a prolonged period of relative depression. The labourers had to accept a cut in their wages. Organised immigration ceased (a state of affairs that continued until the 1850s). By the end of 1843, the artisans and labourers began leaving Nelson; by 1846, some 25% of the immigrants had moved away.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The pressure to find more arable land became intense. To the south-east of Nelson lay the wide and fertile plains of the [Wairau Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairau_Valley "Wairau Valley"), to which the New Zealand Company tried to claim that they had purchased the land. The Māori owners stated adamantly that the Wairau Valley had not formed part of the original land sale, and made it clear they would resist any attempts by the settlers to occupy the area. The Nelson settlers led by Arthur Wakefield and Henry Thompson attempted to do just that. This resulted in the [Wairau Affray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairau_Affray "Wairau Affray"), where 22 settlers and 4 Māori died.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-16) The subsequent Government inquiry exonerated the Māori and found that the Nelson settlers had no legitimate claim to any land outside Tasman Bay.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-17) Public fears of a Māori attack on Nelson led to the formation of the [Nelson Battalion of Militia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Battalion_of_Militia "Nelson Battalion of Militia") in 1845.

### City status

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: City status")]

Nelson township was managed by the [Nelson Provincial Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province") through a Board of Works constituted by the Provincial Government under the Nelson Improvement Act 1856 until 1874. It was proclaimed a Bishop's [See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_see "Episcopal see") and city under letters patent by [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria") on 27 September 1858,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-18) the second New Zealand city proclaimed in this manner after [Christchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch "Christchurch"). Nelson only had some 5,000 residents at this time. [Edmund Hobhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Hobhouse "Edmund Hobhouse")[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-19) was the first Bishop. The Municipal Corporations Act 1876 stated that Nelson was constituted a city on 30 March 1874.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Nelson Province

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Nelson Province")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Nelson_in_New_Zealand_%281852%29.svg/250px-Nelson_in_New_Zealand_%281852%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nelson_in_New_Zealand_(1852).svg)

 The [Nelson Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province") as constituted in 1853

From 1853 until 1876, when provincial governments were abolished, Nelson was the capital of [Nelson Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province"). The province itself was much larger than present-day Nelson City and included all of the present-day [Buller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buller_District "Buller District"), [Kaikōura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaik%C5%8Dura_District "Kaikōura District"), [Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_District "Marlborough District"), Nelson, and Tasman, as well as the [Grey District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_District "Grey District") north of the [Grey River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_River_/_M%C4%81wheranui "Grey River / Māwheranui") and the [Hurunui District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurunui_District "Hurunui District") north of the [Hurunui River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurunui_River "Hurunui River"). The [Marlborough Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Province "Marlborough Province") split from Nelson Province in October 1859.

#### Provincial anniversary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Provincial anniversary")]

[Nelson Anniversary Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Anniversary_Day "Nelson Anniversary Day") is a public holiday observed in the northern half of the South Island of New Zealand, being the area's provincial anniversary day. It is observed throughout the historic Nelson Province, even though the provinces of New Zealand were abolished in 1876. The modern area of observation includes all of Nelson City and includes all of the present-day Buller, Kaikōura, Marlborough, Tasman districts as well as the Grey District north of the Grey River / Māwheranui and the Hurunui District north of the Hurunui River. The holiday usually falls on the Monday closest to 1 February, the anniversary of the arrival of the first New Zealand Company boat, the _Fifeshire_, on 1 February 1842.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-20)

Anniversary celebrations in the early years featured a sailing regatta, horse racing, running races, shooting and ploughing matches. In 1892, the Nelson Jubilee Celebration featured an official week-long programme with church services, sports, concerts, a ball and a grand display of fireworks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### Time gun

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Time gun")]

In 1858, the Nelson Provincial Council erected a [time gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signal#Signal_guns "Time signal") at the spot on Brittania Heights where Captain Wakefield erected his flagpole in 1841. The gun was fired each Saturday at noon to give the correct time. The gun is now preserved as a historical relic and the [Songer Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequoiadendron_giganteum "Sequoiadendron giganteum")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-21) marks the site on Signal Hill of the original flagpole.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-22)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Geography")]

The Nelson-Tasman area comprises two [unitary authorities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_authority "Unitary authority") – Nelson City, administered by the [Nelson City Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_City_Council "Nelson City Council"), and [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District"), administered by the [Tasman District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District_Council "Tasman District Council"), based in [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_New_Zealand "Richmond, New Zealand")15 kilometres (9 miles) to the southwest. It is between [Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Region "Marlborough Region"), another unitary authority, to the east, and the [West Coast Regional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast,_New_Zealand "West Coast, New Zealand") to the west. The Nelson City territorial authority area is small, at only 422 km 2 (163 sq mi).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-23)

For at least two decades, there has been talk about amalgamating Nelson City and the Tasman District to streamline and render more financially economical the existing co-operation between the two councils,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-27) exemplified by the jointly owned [Port Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Nelson,_New_Zealand "Port Nelson, New Zealand") and the jointly funded Nelson Regional Development Agency.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-28) However, an official poll conducted in April 2012 showed nearly three-quarters of those who voted in Tasman were opposed to the proposal, while a majority of Nelson voters were in favour.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-29)

Nelson has beaches and a sheltered harbour. The harbour entrance is protected by a [Boulder Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder_Bank "Boulder Bank"), a natural, 13 km (8 miles) bank of rocks transported south from Mackay Bluff via [longshore drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longshore_drift "Longshore drift"). The bank creates a perfect natural harbour which enticed the first settlers, although the entrance was narrow. The wreck of the _Fifeshire_ on [Arrow Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_Rock,_New_Zealand "Arrow Rock, New Zealand") (now called Fifeshire Rock in memory of this disaster) in 1842 proved the difficulty of the passage.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-30) A cut was later made in the bank in 1906 which allowed larger vessels access to the port.

The creation of Rocks Road around the waterfront area after the [Tāhunanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C4%81hunanui "Tāhunanui") slump[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-31) in 1892 increased the effects of the tide on Nelson city's beach, Tāhunanui, and removed sediment. This meant the popular beach and adjoining car park were being eroded (plus the [sand dunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sand_dunes "Sand dunes")) so a project to replace these sands was put in place and has so far proved a success, with the sand rising a considerable amount and the dunes continuing to grow.

### Waterways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Waterways")]

The Nelson territorial authority area has four main waterways, the [Whangamoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whangamoa_River "Whangamoa River"), [Wakapuaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakapuaka_River "Wakapuaka River"), [Maitai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maitai_River "Maitai River") and [Roding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roding_River "Roding River") Rivers. The Roding River, the southernmost in Nelson, rises in the hills between Mount Meares and [Dun Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dun_Mountain "Dun Mountain"). From there it flows westward before entering the [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District") where it eventually joins the [Waimea River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimea_River_(Tasman) "Waimea River (Tasman)"), which flows into [Waimea Inlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimea_Inlet "Waimea Inlet") near [Moturoa / Rabbit Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moturoa_/_Rabbit_Island "Moturoa / Rabbit Island"). The Maitai River flows westward from the Dun Mountain area into the town centre of Nelson before entering the Nelson Haven then [Tasman Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_Bay "Tasman Bay") via 'The Cut'. Major tributaries of the Maitai River are: [York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Wairepo_/_York_Stream "Te Wairepo / York Stream") and [Brook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brook_Stream,_Nelson "Brook Stream, Nelson") Streams plus [Sharland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharland_Creek "Sharland Creek"), Packer, [Groom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groom_Creek,_Nelson "Groom Creek, Nelson"), Glen, Neds, Sclanders, Beauchamp and Mill Creeks. The Wakapuaka River, which flows north from the Saddle Hill area to its mouth at [Cable Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_Bay "Cable Bay") in North Nelson, has two main tributaries, the Lud and Teal Rivers. Entering Tasman Bay near Kokorua in the north of Nelson, the Whangamoa River is the longest waterway in Nelson. Smaller waterways in the south of Nelson include: Saxton Creek, Orchard Stream, Poorman Valley Stream, Arapiki Stream, Jenkins Creek and Maire Stream.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-33)

### Central city

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Central city")]

The central city of Nelson, also referred to as the central business district (CBD), is bounded by Halifax Street to the north, Rutherford Street to the west, Collingwood Street to the east, and Selwyn Place to the south.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-34) Other major streets within the CBD include Trafalgar Street, Bridge Street and Hardy Street.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Climate")]

Nelson has a temperate [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") ([Cfb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")), with cool winters and warm summers. Nelson has rainfall evenly distributed throughout the year and has fewer frosts due to the highly marine geography of New Zealand. Winter is the stormiest time, where gales and storms are more common. Nelson has one of the sunniest climates of all major New Zealand centres,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-royalsociety.org.nz-37) earning the nickname 'Sunny Nelson' with an annual average total of over 2400 hours of sunshine.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-38) The highest recorded temperature in Nelson is 36.3°C (97°F), the lowest −6.6°C (20°F).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### "Centre of New Zealand" monument

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: \"Centre of New Zealand\" monument")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Geographical_centre_nelson.jpg/250px-Geographical_centre_nelson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Geographical_centre_nelson.jpg)

The marker at the "Centre of New Zealand"

Nelson has a monument on Botanical Hill, near the centre of the city. The walk to this is called the "_Centre of New Zealand walk_". Despite the name, this monument does not mark the actual geographic centre of New Zealand.

Instead, the monument marks the "zero, zero" point to which the first geodetic surveys of New Zealand were referenced. These surveys were started in the 1870s by John Spence Browning, the Chief Surveyor for Nelson. From this 360-degree viewpoint, survey marks in neighbouring regions (including Wellington in the North Island) could be [triangulated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangulation "Triangulation") and the local surveys connected.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-42)

In 1962, Ian Reilly from the now defunct [Department of Scientific and Industrial Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_(New_Zealand) "Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)") calculated the geographic centre of New Zealand (including Stewart Island and some smaller islands in addition to the North and South Island, but excluding the [Chathams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Islands "Chatham Islands")) to be in a forest in [Spooners Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spooner's_Range,_New_Zealand?action=edit&redlink=1 "Spooner's Range, New Zealand (page does not exist)")35 mi (56 kilometres) southwest of Nelson at [41°30′S 172°50′E / 41.500°S 172.833°E / -41.500; 172.833 (Geographical Centre of New Zealand)](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Nelson,_New_Zealand&params=41_30_S_172_50_E_region:NZ_type:landmark&title=Geographical+Centre+of+New+Zealand).[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-43)

Owing to the coarse nature of the underlying data (use of rectangular areas of 7.5 minutes of arc on each side), the centre calculated by Reilly has quite large error margins. Recalculating the result with more modern and accurate data shows the geographic centre of New Zealand is approximately 60 km southwest of Nelson, in the Big Bush Conservation Area north of [Saint Arnaud, New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Arnaud,_New_Zealand "Saint Arnaud, New Zealand").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-44)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Government")]

### Local

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Local")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Nelson_City_Council_Building.JPG/250px-Nelson_City_Council_Building.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nelson_City_Council_Building.JPG)

The Nelson City Council building in 2012

As a [unitary authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_authority "Unitary authority"), the [Nelson City Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_City_Council "Nelson City Council") has the combined responsibilities and functions of both a [territorial (local)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_authorities_of_New_Zealand "Territorial authorities of New Zealand") and [regional council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_New_Zealand "Regions of New Zealand"). This is different from most other local authorities in New Zealand. More often, a regional council is a separate organisation with several territorial authorities (city or district councils) within its borders. Other unitary authorities are the [Auckland Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Council "Auckland Council"), [Gisborne District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gisborne_District_Council "Gisborne District Council"), [Marlborough District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Region "Marlborough Region"), [Tasman District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District_Council "Tasman District Council") and the [Chatham Islands Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Islands_Council "Chatham Islands Council").

The Nelson City Council holds elections for the [mayor of Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Nelson,_New_Zealand "Mayor of Nelson, New Zealand") and 12 councillors under the [STV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_Transferable_Voting "Single Transferable Voting") electoral system every three years. As of 12 October 2025, the mayor is [Nick Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Smith_(New_Zealand_politician) "Nick Smith (New Zealand politician)").

Nelson City has a coat of arms, obtained in 1958 from the [College of Arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Arms "College of Arms") to mark the centenary of Nelson as a city. The [blazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blazon "Blazon") of the arms is:

"Barry wavy Argent and Azure a Cross Flory Sable on a Chief also Azure a Mitre proper And for the Crest on a Wreath of the Colours Issuant from a Mural Crown proper a Lion rampant Gules holding between the fore paws a Sun in splendour or. The supporters on the dexter side a Huia Bird and on the sinister side a Kotuku both proper."
Motto "_Palmam qui meruit ferat_" (Let him who has earned it bear the palm). This motto is the same as that of [Lord Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Nelson "Horatio Nelson").

### National

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: National")]

Nelson is covered by the [Nelson general electorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_(New_Zealand_electorate) "Nelson (New Zealand electorate)"), and the [Te Tai Tonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Tai_Tonga "Te Tai Tonga") Māori electorate, which covers the entire South Island and part of [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington") in the North Island. Since the [2023 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_New_Zealand_general_election "2023 New Zealand general election"), Nelson is held by [Rachel Boyack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Boyack "Rachel Boyack") of the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Labour_Party "New Zealand Labour Party"), and Te Tai Tonga by [Tākuta Ferris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C4%81kuta_Ferris "Tākuta Ferris") of [Te Pāti Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_P%C4%81ti_M%C4%81ori "Te Pāti Māori").

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Economy")]

The Nelson economy (and that of the neighbouring [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District")) is based on the 'big five' industries; seafood, horticulture, forestry, farming and tourism.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-54) Port Nelson[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-55) is the biggest fishing port in [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia "Australasia"). There are also a range of growth industries, including art and craft, aviation, [engineering technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering_technology "Engineering technology"), and information technology. The region was sixth in terms of GDP growth in the 2007–10 period.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-stuff.co.nz-56)

The combined sub-national GDP of Nelson and Tasman District was estimated at $3.4 billion in 2010, 1.8% of New Zealand's national GDP.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-stuff.co.nz-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-57)

The Nelson Regional Development Agency is an economic development agency for Nelson and the Tasman District.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-58)

Some of the region's largest companies and employers are:

*   [Helicopters (NZ)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopters_(NZ) "Helicopters (NZ)") has its headquarters and maintenance base at [Nelson Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Airport_(New_Zealand) "Nelson Airport (New Zealand)").
*   Japanese automobile manufacturer [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda "Honda") has its New Zealand distribution centre in the Whakatu Industrial Estate in [Stoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke,_New_Zealand "Stoke, New Zealand").
*   Beverage company [McCashins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCashins_Brewery "McCashins Brewery") has a [microbrewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbrewery "Microbrewery") in Stoke.
*   SeaDragon Marine Oils[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-59) has a fish oil refinery in Annesbrook.
*   The [Cawthron Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cawthron_Institute "Cawthron Institute") has a research facility in [The Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wood,_New_Zealand "The Wood, New Zealand").
*   Food manufacturer the [Talley's Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talley's_Group "Talley's Group") has processing facilities at [Port Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Nelson,_New_Zealand "Port Nelson, New Zealand").
*   New Zealand King Salmon processes [Chinook salmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_salmon "Chinook salmon") at its factory in [Annesbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annesbrook "Annesbrook").
*   [Pic's Peanut Butter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pic's_Peanut_Butter "Pic's Peanut Butter") is made in its Stoke factory.

Former regional airline [Air Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Nelson "Air Nelson") had its headquarters and maintenance base at Nelson Airport.

In 2013, Nelson Mayor [Aldo Miccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Miccio "Aldo Miccio") worked on a proposal that would see Australian [call centres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_centres "Call centres") for companies such as [Gen-i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen-i "Gen-i") and [Xero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xero_(software) "Xero (software)") relocated to Nelson. The plan was in response to Australian companies moving call and contact centres out of Asia because their Australian customers preferred English-speaking centres. If the plan was successful, Miccio expected 100 to 300 jobs paying NZ$50,000-plus in the first year to be created in Nelson.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-60)

### Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Tourism")]

Nelson is a gateway for tourists and visitors exploring the [Abel Tasman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Tasman_National_Park "Abel Tasman National Park"), [Kahurangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kahurangi_National_Park "Kahurangi National Park"), and [Nelson Lakes National Parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Lakes_National_Park "Nelson Lakes National Park"), and the [Great Taste Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Taste_Trail "Great Taste Trail"), and popular walks such as the [Abel Tasman Coast Track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Tasman_Coast_Track "Abel Tasman Coast Track"), and [Heaphy Track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaphy_Track "Heaphy Track").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-61)

It is a centre for both [ecotourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecotourism "Ecotourism") and [adventure tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_travel "Adventure travel") and has a high reputation among [caving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave "Cave") enthusiasts due to several prominent cave systems around [Takaka Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takaka_Hill "Takaka Hill") and the [Wharepapa / Arthur Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharepapa_/_Arthur_Range "Wharepapa / Arthur Range"), including the [Nettlebed Cave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nettlebed_Cave "Nettlebed Cave") and some of the largest and deepest explored caverns in the Southern Hemisphere.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Suter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Suter "Andrew Suter") Art Gallery, before its 2017 renovation

These include [potters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottery "Pottery"), [glass blowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glassblowing "Glassblowing"), and dozens of [wood carvers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood_carving "Wood carving") using native New Zealand [southern beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_beech "Southern beech") and exotic _Cupressus macrocarpa._[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-63)

### Marae

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Marae")]

Whakatū Marae, in the suburb of [Atawhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atawhai "Atawhai"), is the _[marae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marae "Marae")_ (meeting ground) of [Ngāti Kuia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Kuia "Ngāti Kuia"), [Ngāti Kōata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_K%C5%8Data "Ngāti Kōata"), [Ngāti Rārua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_R%C4%81rua "Ngāti Rārua"), [Ngāti Tama ki Te Tau Ihu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Tama_ki_Te_Tau_Ihu "Ngāti Tama ki Te Tau Ihu"), [Ngāti Toa Rangatira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Toa_Rangatira "Ngāti Toa Rangatira") and [Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Atiawa_o_Te_Waka-a-M%C4%81ui "Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui"). It includes the Kākāti _[wharenui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharenui "Wharenui")_ (meeting house). In October 2020, the Government committed $240,739 from the [Provincial Growth Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provincial_Growth_Fund "Provincial Growth Fund") to restore the marae, creating an estimated 9 jobs.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-maraepgf-75)

### Museums

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Museums")]

[Founders Heritage Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founders_Heritage_Park "Founders Heritage Park") is an interactive park that shows the history of Nelson. The park is set up as a village filled with buildings set in a historical time, including well established gardens. Throughout the park, there are stories to be learned about the history of this town.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-76) It houses a number of groups with historical themes, including transport.

The [Nelson Provincial Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Provincial_Museum "Nelson Provincial Museum") houses a collection of locally significant artefacts. The [Nelson Classic Car Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Classic_Car_Museum?action=edit&redlink=1 "Nelson Classic Car Museum (page does not exist)") is home to a collection of more than 150 historical collectable cars, making it one of the largest automobile museums in the country.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-77)

### Parks and zoo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Parks and zoo")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Founders_Heritage_Park_main_street.jpg/250px-Founders_Heritage_Park_main_street.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Founders_Heritage_Park_main_street.jpg)

Founders Heritage Park

Nelson has a large number and variety of [public parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_parks "Public parks") and reserves maintained at public expense by the City Council.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-78) Major reserves include Grampians Reserve, close to the suburb of [Braemar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braemar,_New_Zealand?action=edit&redlink=1 "Braemar, New Zealand (page does not exist)"), and the [Botanical Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanical_Gardens,_Nelson "Botanical Gardens, Nelson") in the east of Nelson, close to [The Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wood,_New_Zealand "The Wood, New Zealand").

[Natureland Wildlife Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natureland_Wildlife_Trust?action=edit&redlink=1 "Natureland Wildlife Trust (page does not exist)") (formerly Natureland Zoological Park) is a small zoological facility close to Tāhunanui Beach. The facility is popular with children, where they can closely approach animals such as: [monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey "Monkey") (black-capped capuchins, cotton-top tamarins and pygmy marmosets), [lemurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemur "Lemur"), [meerkats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meerkat "Meerkat"), [agoutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agouti "Agouti"), [porcupines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcupine "Porcupine"), [llamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Llama "Llama"), [alpacas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpaca "Alpaca"), [Kune Kune pigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunekune "Kunekune") and [peacocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacocks "Peacocks"). There are also [green iguanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_iguana "Green iguana"), [tropical fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_fish "Tropical fish"), [kākās](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81k%C4%81 "Kākā"), [keas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kea "Kea") and other birds including in a walk through [aviary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviary "Aviary").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-79) Although the zoo nearly closed in 2008, the Orana Wildlife Trust took over its running instead.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-80) It looked like[_[to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_] a bright future ahead for Natureland and its staff, but since the repeated earthquakes in [Christchurch in 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Christchurch_earthquake "2011 Christchurch earthquake") and the damage to Orana Park, Orana Wildlife Trust are uncertain of the future of Natureland.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-81) Orana Wildlife Trust have since pulled out of Natureland, which is now run independently.

### Symphony orchestra

### Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

### Law enforcement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Law enforcement")]

The [Nelson Central Police Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Police "New Zealand Police"), located in St John Street, is the headquarters for the Tasman Police District.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-105) In 2012/2013 the Tasman Police District had the lowest crime rate within New Zealand.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-106)

Several [gangs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang "Gang") and [biker clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_motorcycle_club "Outlaw motorcycle club") have established themselves in Nelson. They include the now disbanded [Lost Breed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Breed "Lost Breed") and the [Red Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Devils_Motorcycle_Club "Red Devils Motorcycle Club") (a support club for the [Hells Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hells_Angels "Hells Angels")). The [Rebels Motorcycle Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebels_Motorcycle_Club "Rebels Motorcycle Club") also has a presence in the wider Nelson-Tasman area.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-107)

### Electricity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Electricity")]

The Nelson City Municipal Electricity Department (MED) established the city's public electricity supply in 1923, with electricity generated by a coal-fired power station at Wakefield Quay. The city was connected to the newly commissioned [Cobb hydroelectric power station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobb_Power_Station "Cobb Power Station") in 1944 and to the rest of the South Island grid in 1958. The grid connection saw the Wakefield Quay power station was relegated to standby duty before being decommissioned in 1964.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Nelson_Electricity_Ltd,_New_Zealand-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-109)

Today, Nelson Electricity operates the local distribution network in the former MED area, which covers the CBD and inner suburbs, while Network Tasman operates the local distribution network in the outer suburbs (including Stoke, Tāhunanui and Atawhai) and the nearby rural areas.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Nelson_Electricity_Ltd,_New_Zealand-108)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-110)

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Transport")]

### Air transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Air transport")]

[Nelson Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Airport_(New_Zealand) "Nelson Airport (New Zealand)") is at [Annesbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annesbrook "Annesbrook"), an industrial suburb southwest of the central city. It operates a single terminal and 1,347-metre (4,419-foot) runway. About a million passengers use the airport annually and it was the [fifth-busiest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_New_Zealand "List of the busiest airports in New Zealand") airport in New Zealand by passenger numbers in 2024. It is primarily used for domestic flights, with regular flights to and from [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland"), [Christchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch "Christchurch"), [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_New_Zealand "Hamilton, New Zealand"), [Kāpiti Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Coast "Kāpiti Coast"), [Palmerston North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmerston_North "Palmerston North") and [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington"). [Sounds Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounds_Air "Sounds Air") offers flights to and from Wellington. In 2006, it received restricted international airport status to facilitate small private jets.

The airport was home to [Air Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Nelson "Air Nelson"), which operated and maintained New Zealand's largest domestic airline fleet, and is now merged into [Air New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_New_Zealand "Air New Zealand"). It was also the headquarters of [Origin Pacific Airways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_Pacific_Airways "Origin Pacific Airways") until its collapse in 2006.

In February 2018, the approach road to the airport was flooded when the adjoining Jenkins Creek burst its banks during a storm that brought king tides and strong winds. The airport was closed for about one hour.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-111) In 2022, the NZ SeaRise programme identified Nelson airport as an area of particular vulnerability to [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise_in_New_Zealand "Sea level rise in New Zealand"), with a projected subsidence of 5 millimetres (0.20 in) per year.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Bradnock-2022-112) The airport's chief executive said that the proposed runway extension would be planned around the latest sea level rise forecast, and that the airport was "here to stay", despite the concerns over the threats posed by sea level rise.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Bradnock-2022-112)

**Nelson** ([Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language "Māori language"): _Whakatū_) is a [city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_New_Zealand "List of cities in New Zealand") and [unitary authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_New_Zealand "Districts of New Zealand") on the eastern shores of the [Tasman Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_Bay "Tasman Bay") at the top of the [South Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Island "South Island") of New Zealand. It is the oldest city in the South Island and the second-oldest settled city in the country; it was established in 1841 and became a city by British [royal charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter") in 1858.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-TeAra_places1-3)

Nelson City is bordered to the west and south-west by the [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District") and to the north-east, east and south-east by the [Marlborough District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_District "Marlborough District"). The Nelson urban area has a population of 50,800,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-NZ_population_data_2018-1) making it New Zealand's 15th [most populous urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_populated_places_in_New_Zealand "List of populated places in New Zealand").

Nelson is well known for its thriving local arts and crafts scene; each year, the city hosts events popular with locals and tourists alike, such as the Nelson Arts Festival.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-4)

## Naming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Naming")]

Nelson was named in honour of Admiral [Horatio Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Nelson,_1st_Viscount_Nelson "Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson"), who defeated both the [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_French_Empire "First French Empire") and [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") fleets at the [Battle of Trafalgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Trafalgar "Battle of Trafalgar") in October 1805. Many roads and public areas around the city are named after people and ships associated with that battle. Inhabitants of the city are referred to as "Nelsonians". Trafalgar Street is its main shopping axis.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Nelson's [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language "Māori language") name, _Whakatū_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Maori-5) means 'construct', 'raise', or 'establish'.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-6)

In an article to _The Colonist_ newspaper on 16 July 1867, Francis Stevens described Nelson as "The [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples") of the [Southern Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere "Southern Hemisphere")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-7) Today, Nelson is nicknamed "Sunny Nelson" due to its high sunshine hours per year and the "Top of the South" because of its geographic location.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [New Zealand Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Sign_Language "New Zealand Sign Language"), the name is signed by putting the index and middle fingers together, which are raised to the nose until the fingertips touch the nose, then move the hand forward so that the fingers point slightly forward away from oneself.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-8)

### Māori settlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Māori settlement")]

Settlement of Nelson began about 700 years ago by [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_people "Māori people").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-9) There is evidence that the earliest settlements in New Zealand were around the Nelson–Marlborough regions. Some of the earliest recorded [iwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iwi "Iwi") in the Nelson district are Ngāti Hāwea, Ngāti Wairangi, [Waitaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitaha_(South_Island_iwi) "Waitaha (South Island iwi)") and [Kāti Māmoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81ti_M%C4%81moe "Kāti Māmoe").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10) Waitaha people developed the land around the Waimea Gardens, are believed to have been the first people to quarry [argillite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argillite "Argillite") in around Nelson. They also developed much of the Waimea Gardens complex – more than 400 hectares (990 acres) on the Waimea Plains near Nelson.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Te_Tau-11) In the early 1600s, [Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_T%C5%ABmatak%C5%8Dkiri "Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri") displaced other [te Tau Ihu Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Tau_Ihu_M%C4%81ori "Te Tau Ihu Māori"), becoming the dominant tribe in the area until the early 1800s.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10) Raids from northern tribes in the 1820s, led by [Te Rauparaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Rauparaha "Te Rauparaha") and his [Ngāti Toa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Toa "Ngāti Toa"), soon decimated the local population and quickly displaced them.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Today, there are eight mutually recognised tribes of the northwestern region: [Ngāti Kuia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Kuia "Ngāti Kuia"), [Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Apa_ki_te_R%C4%81_T%C5%8D "Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō"), [Rangitāne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangit%C4%81ne "Rangitāne"), [Ngāti Toarangatira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Toa "Ngāti Toa"), [Ngāti Koata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Koata "Ngāti Koata"), [Ngāti Rārua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_R%C4%81rua "Ngāti Rārua"), [Ngāti Tama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ti_Tama "Ngāti Tama") and [Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Atiawa_o_Te_Waka-a-M%C4%81ui "Te Atiawa o Te Waka-a-Māui").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-Walrond-10)

### New Zealand Company and European settlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: New Zealand Company and European settlement")]

#### Planning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Planning")]

The [New Zealand Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Company "New Zealand Company") in London planned the settlement of Nelson. They intended to buy from the Māori some 200,000 acres (810 km 2) of land, which they planned to divide into one thousand lots and sell to intending settlers. The company earmarked profits to finance the free passage of [artisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artisan "Artisan") and [labourers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laborer "Laborer"), with their families, and for the construction of public works. However, by September 1841 only about one third of the lots had sold. Despite this, the colony pushed ahead, and land was surveyed by [Frederick Tuckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Tuckett "Frederick Tuckett").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-DNZB_Tuckett-12)

Three ships, the _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Arrow "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Whitby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Whitby "New Zealand Company ships")_, and _[Will Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Will\_Watch "New Zealand Company ships")_, sailed from London, the expedition commanded by Captain [Arthur Wakefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Wakefield "Arthur Wakefield"). Arriving in New Zealand, they discovered that the new Governor of the colony, [William Hobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hobson "William Hobson"), would not give them a free hand to secure vast areas of land from the Māori or indeed to decide where to site the colony. However, after some delay, Hobson allowed the company to investigate the Tasman Bay area at the north end of the South Island. The Company selected the site now occupied by Nelson City because it had the best harbour in the area. But it had a major drawback: it lacked suitable [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land "Arable land"); Nelson City stands right on the edge of a mountain range while the nearby Waimea Plains amount to only about 60,000 acres (240 km 2), less than one third of the area required by the Company plans.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Company secured land, which was not clearly defined, from the Māori for £800: it included Nelson, Waimea, [Motueka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motueka "Motueka"), [Riwaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riwaka "Riwaka") and Whakapuaka. This allowed the settlement to begin, but the lack of definition would prove the source of much future conflict. The three colony ships sailed into Nelson Haven during the first week of November 1841. When the first four immigrant ships – _[Fifeshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Fifeshire "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Mary-Ann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Mary\_Anne "New Zealand Company ships")_, _[Lord Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Lord\_Auckland "New Zealand Company ships")_ and _[Lloyds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Zealand\_Company\_ships#Lloyds "New Zealand Company ships")_ – arrived three months later, they found the town already laid out with streets, some wooden houses, tents and rough sheds. The town was laid out on a [grid plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan "Grid plan").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-13) Within 18 months, the company had sent out 18 ships with 1,052 men, 872 women and 1,384 children. However, fewer than ninety of the settlers had the capital to start as landowners.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### Cultural and religious immigrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cultural and religious immigrants")]

The early settlement of Nelson province included a proportion of [German immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_New_Zealanders "German New Zealanders"), who arrived on the ship _Sankt Pauli_ and formed the nucleus of the villages of Sarau ([Upper Moutere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Moutere "Upper Moutere")) and Neudorf. These were mostly [Lutheran Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism") with a small number of [Bavarian Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bavarians "Bavarians").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-14)

In 1892, the [New Zealand Church Missionary Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Church_Missionary_Society "New Zealand Church Missionary Society") (NZCMS) was formed in a Nelson church hall.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-NZCMS-Mission-15)

#### Problems with land

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Problems with land")]

After a brief initial period of prosperity, the lack of land and of capital caught up with the settlement and it entered a prolonged period of relative depression. The labourers had to accept a cut in their wages. Organised immigration ceased (a state of affairs that continued until the 1850s). By the end of 1843, the artisans and labourers began leaving Nelson; by 1846, some 25% of the immigrants had moved away.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The pressure to find more arable land became intense. To the south-east of Nelson lay the wide and fertile plains of the [Wairau Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairau_Valley "Wairau Valley"), to which the New Zealand Company tried to claim that they had purchased the land. The Māori owners stated adamantly that the Wairau Valley had not formed part of the original land sale, and made it clear they would resist any attempts by the settlers to occupy the area. The Nelson settlers led by Arthur Wakefield and Henry Thompson attempted to do just that. This resulted in the [Wairau Affray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairau_Affray "Wairau Affray"), where 22 settlers and 4 Māori died.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-16) The subsequent Government inquiry exonerated the Māori and found that the Nelson settlers had no legitimate claim to any land outside Tasman Bay.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-17) Public fears of a Māori attack on Nelson led to the formation of the [Nelson Battalion of Militia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Battalion_of_Militia "Nelson Battalion of Militia") in 1845.

### City status

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: City status")]

Nelson township was managed by the [Nelson Provincial Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province") through a Board of Works constituted by the Provincial Government under the Nelson Improvement Act 1856 until 1874. It was proclaimed a Bishop's [See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_see "Episcopal see") and city under letters patent by [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria") on 27 September 1858,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-18) the second New Zealand city proclaimed in this manner after [Christchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch "Christchurch"). Nelson only had some 5,000 residents at this time. [Edmund Hobhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Hobhouse "Edmund Hobhouse")[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-19) was the first Bishop. The Municipal Corporations Act 1876 stated that Nelson was constituted a city on 30 March 1874.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Nelson Province

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Nelson Province")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Nelson_in_New_Zealand_%281852%29.svg/250px-Nelson_in_New_Zealand_%281852%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nelson_in_New_Zealand_(1852).svg)

 The [Nelson Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province") as constituted in 1853

From 1853 until 1876, when provincial governments were abolished, Nelson was the capital of [Nelson Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Province "Nelson Province"). The province itself was much larger than present-day Nelson City and included all of the present-day [Buller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buller_District "Buller District"), [Kaikōura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaik%C5%8Dura_District "Kaikōura District"), [Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_District "Marlborough District"), Nelson, and Tasman, as well as the [Grey District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_District "Grey District") north of the [Grey River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_River_/_M%C4%81wheranui "Grey River / Māwheranui") and the [Hurunui District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurunui_District "Hurunui District") north of the [Hurunui River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurunui_River "Hurunui River"). The [Marlborough Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Province "Marlborough Province") split from Nelson Province in October 1859.

#### Provincial anniversary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Provincial anniversary")]

[Nelson Anniversary Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Anniversary_Day "Nelson Anniversary Day") is a public holiday observed in the northern half of the South Island of New Zealand, being the area's provincial anniversary day. It is observed throughout the historic Nelson Province, even though the provinces of New Zealand were abolished in 1876. The modern area of observation includes all of Nelson City and includes all of the present-day Buller, Kaikōura, Marlborough, Tasman districts as well as the Grey District north of the Grey River / Māwheranui and the Hurunui District north of the Hurunui River. The holiday usually falls on the Monday closest to 1 February, the anniversary of the arrival of the first New Zealand Company boat, the _Fifeshire_, on 1 February 1842.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-20)

Anniversary celebrations in the early years featured a sailing regatta, horse racing, running races, shooting and ploughing matches. In 1892, the Nelson Jubilee Celebration featured an official week-long programme with church services, sports, concerts, a ball and a grand display of fireworks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### Time gun

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Time gun")]

In 1858, the Nelson Provincial Council erected a [time gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signal#Signal_guns "Time signal") at the spot on Brittania Heights where Captain Wakefield erected his flagpole in 1841. The gun was fired each Saturday at noon to give the correct time. The gun is now preserved as a historical relic and the [Songer Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequoiadendron_giganteum "Sequoiadendron giganteum")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-21) marks the site on Signal Hill of the original flagpole.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-22)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Geography")]

The Nelson-Tasman area comprises two [unitary authorities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_authority "Unitary authority") – Nelson City, administered by the [Nelson City Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_City_Council "Nelson City Council"), and [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District"), administered by the [Tasman District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District_Council "Tasman District Council"), based in [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_New_Zealand "Richmond, New Zealand")15 kilometres (9 miles) to the southwest. It is between [Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Region "Marlborough Region"), another unitary authority, to the east, and the [West Coast Regional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast,_New_Zealand "West Coast, New Zealand") to the west. The Nelson City territorial authority area is small, at only 422 km 2 (163 sq mi).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-23)

For at least two decades, there has been talk about amalgamating Nelson City and the Tasman District to streamline and render more financially economical the existing co-operation between the two councils,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-27) exemplified by the jointly owned [Port Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Nelson,_New_Zealand "Port Nelson, New Zealand") and the jointly funded Nelson Regional Development Agency.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-28) However, an official poll conducted in April 2012 showed nearly three-quarters of those who voted in Tasman were opposed to the proposal, while a majority of Nelson voters were in favour.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-29)

Nelson has beaches and a sheltered harbour. The harbour entrance is protected by a [Boulder Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder_Bank "Boulder Bank"), a natural, 13 km (8 miles) bank of rocks transported south from Mackay Bluff via [longshore drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longshore_drift "Longshore drift"). The bank creates a perfect natural harbour which enticed the first settlers, although the entrance was narrow. The wreck of the _Fifeshire_ on [Arrow Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_Rock,_New_Zealand "Arrow Rock, New Zealand") (now called Fifeshire Rock in memory of this disaster) in 1842 proved the difficulty of the passage.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-30) A cut was later made in the bank in 1906 which allowed larger vessels access to the port.

The creation of Rocks Road around the waterfront area after the [Tāhunanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C4%81hunanui "Tāhunanui") slump[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-31) in 1892 increased the effects of the tide on Nelson city's beach, Tāhunanui, and removed sediment. This meant the popular beach and adjoining car park were being eroded (plus the [sand dunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sand_dunes "Sand dunes")) so a project to replace these sands was put in place and has so far proved a success, with the sand rising a considerable amount and the dunes continuing to grow.

### Waterways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Waterways")]

The Nelson territorial authority area has four main waterways, the [Whangamoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whangamoa_River "Whangamoa River"), [Wakapuaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakapuaka_River "Wakapuaka River"), [Maitai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maitai_River "Maitai River") and [Roding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roding_River "Roding River") Rivers. The Roding River, the southernmost in Nelson, rises in the hills between Mount Meares and [Dun Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dun_Mountain "Dun Mountain"). From there it flows westward before entering the [Tasman District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_District "Tasman District") where it eventually joins the [Waimea River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimea_River_(Tasman) "Waimea River (Tasman)"), which flows into [Waimea Inlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimea_Inlet "Waimea Inlet") near [Moturoa / Rabbit Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moturoa_/_Rabbit_Island "Moturoa / Rabbit Island"). The Maitai River flows westward from the Dun Mountain area into the town centre of Nelson before entering the Nelson Haven then [Tasman Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_Bay "Tasman Bay") via 'The Cut'. Major tributaries of the Maitai River are: [York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Wairepo_/_York_Stream "Te Wairepo / York Stream") and [Brook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brook_Stream,_Nelson "Brook Stream, Nelson") Streams plus [Sharland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharland_Creek "Sharland Creek"), Packer, [Groom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groom_Creek,_Nelson "Groom Creek, Nelson"), Glen, Neds, Sclanders, Beauchamp and Mill Creeks. The Wakapuaka River, which flows north from the Saddle Hill area to its mouth at [Cable Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_Bay "Cable Bay") in North Nelson, has two main tributaries, the Lud and Teal Rivers. Entering Tasman Bay near Kokorua in the north of Nelson, the Whangamoa River is the longest waterway in Nelson. Smaller waterways in the south of Nelson include: Saxton Creek, Orchard Stream, Poorman Valley Stream, Arapiki Stream, Jenkins Creek and Maire Stream.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-33)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nelson,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Climate")]

Nelson has a temperate [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") ([Cfb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")), with cool winters and warm summers. Nelson has rainfall evenly distributed throughout the year and has fewer frosts due to the highly marine geography of New Zealand. Winter is the stormiest time, where gales and storms are more common. Nelson has one of the sunniest climates of all major New Zealand centres,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-royalsociety.org.nz-37) earning the nickname 'Sunny Nelson' with an annual average total of over 2400 hours of sunshine.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson,_New_Zealand#cite_note-38) The highest recorded temperature in Nelson is 36.3°C (97°F), the lowest −6.6°C (20°F).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
